findings.summary: G1's new paragraph says every gate 'imports, calls or reads no module, function, file or label the brief leaves open'. Read literally, that also forbids the gate's own fixtures: the files in .vloop/state/gates/<task id>/ and the temporary files a gate builds. The brief names neither. P-4 makes the gate folder part of the planner's judge, and the plan skill tells the planner to use it. A literal model, which is exactly the reader this brief targets (gpt-6.1-terra already wrote no gate folder), can read the new sentence as one more reason to avoid the folder, or as a contradiction of the skill's gate-folder guidance. The forbidden set is the implementation's names, not every name the brief leaves open.
findings.evidence: Brief G1 quoted paragraph; docs/domain/domain-model.md:197-198 (P-4: 'A gate's judge is the planner's — its verify and its gate folder'); docs/design-notes/copilot-cli-experiments.md:583-584 ('No gate folder again, as with 5.6').
findings.fix: Scope the clause to the work: '... and imports, calls or reads no module, function, file or label of the implementation that the brief leaves open (its own fixtures and gate folder aside)'. Or use equivalent fixed text, and update the worked example's grep lines if they quote the changed words (today they do not).

decisions: Fix the plan skill rather than the gate review's pins-unnamed standard: agree; the 2026-11-02 run shows the gate review was right.
A pin stays possible only where no named surface reaches the criterion, and it is stated in the task's acceptance: agree. The gate review reads state.json, not the plan's report.
G1 drops the old sentence 'Do not pin a name that no gate uses.', which 'pin the minimum a gate needs, and no more' now covers: fine, but the operator should know the sentence goes.
G2 is skill text only, with no driver check (out of scope). The eval does not exercise a revision round, so only acceptance 2 tests G2: acceptable.
The gate-review ceiling goes from 1550 to 1600 (1527 now, about 1556 after the sentence); plan stays at 4100 (3804 now, about 3900 after): agree.

The eval's brief forbids a gate folder ('each task's judge is its verify command alone') because the llm grader's single focus is state.json. Sound, but it is still not in 'Decided here' (rounds 2 and 3 noted it too); one line there would make it visible.
The new scaffold writes no .vloop/state/, unlike both plan scaffolds it is modelled on: harmless, since Write creates the directory, but it is a quiet difference.
A shell library, so the case needs only sh: fine.
No domain invariant changes; P-4 and P-8 already hold the principle: agree.
gpt-6.1-terra is the only candidate, and the others wait for #81: fine.
Qualification is the operator's acceptance at close, and the PR closes #84 only if every phase qualifies: necessary.
The whole brief was written under the operator's delegation of 2026-11-02 for the #81-#88 chain: the operator should confirm the delegation covers marking it ready.
